chunks: And from him, from his father, from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, from Qutayba, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

When you are behind an Imam whom you are pleased with, in a prayer wherein the recitation is made loud, and you do not hear his recitation, then you recite for yourself; and if you hear the humming (of the Imam), then do not recite.

key_terms.الْقِرَاءَة: Recitation (specifically of Al-Fatihah and another Surah)
key_terms.يُجْهَرُ فِيهَا بِالْقِرَاءَةِ: Loud recitation (referring to prayers where the Imam recites audibly)

ai.seo_question: When should a follower recite Al-Fatihah behind the Imam in loud prayers?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the condition of 'hearing' (samt) as the determinant for the follower's obligation to recite Surah Al-Fatihah independently during prayers with loud recitation (jahriyyah). It reflects the Shia juristic emphasis on the physical audibility of the Imam's recitation, distinguishing between clear hearing and mere perception of murmuring, thereby ensuring the validity of the individual's prayer component.

en.hubeali:
And from him, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, from Quteyba, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘When you were behind a Imam you are pleased with in a Salāt wherein is loud recitation, but you cannot hear his recitation, so recite to yourself; but if you can hear the humming (of the Imam), so do not recite’.
en.sarwar: 4. It is a narration from him (narrator of previous Hadith) by his father from ‘Abd Allah ibn al-Mughirah from Qutaybah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, has said, ‘

When you perform Salah (prayer) behind an Imam and are happy with him in Salah (prayer) of which recitation is to be read aloud and you do not hear his recitation, then recite to yourself, but if you hear a humming sound, do not recite.’”
